schema_fields.description: Whether derivative spikes in dL/dt are physical phenomena (true) or instrumental artifacts (false). Physical spikes represent real material responses: rapid hydrogen absorption/desorption events, phase transformation kinetics, or structural relaxation processes. These correlate with features in the Delta L(t) curve and are reproducible across replicate measurements. Instrumental spikes are measurement artifacts: electrical noise, mechanical vibrations, digitization errors, or sensor drift. These appear as random high-frequency fluctuations uncorrelated with the underlying dilatation trend and vary between replicates. In dilatometry, most high-frequency spikes in dL/dt that require smoothing are instrumental, while smooth rate changes reflecting Delta L features are physical.

cases.system_answer: Yes. The measurement setup (dilatometry with time-resolved length change and derivative analysis) can observe α-to-β phase transformation in Pd–H in the absence of a miscibility gap. Without a miscibility gap, the transformation manifests as continuous, monotonic behavior in the thermal expansion derivative (dL/dt); with a gap, sharp discontinuities or localized peaks appear. All three records show derivative_validation=true and adequate signal-to-noise ratios (39.37–39.47), confirming the setup has sufficient sensitivity to detect both signatures. Records 001 and 002 exhibit smoothed_derivative_monotonic=true, consistent with continuous transformation; record_003 shows derivative_spikes_physical=true, consistent with discontinuous behavior. The setup is capable of making this thermodynamic distinction.
